This directory standardises the three-letter site codes used in work orders, travel

------------------------------------------------------------------

To: All Staff
From: Finance Department
Date: 15 March 2026
Re: Per Diem Policy – Clarifications and Reminders

Following a review of expense claims submitted in January and February 2026, the Finance Department wishes to clarify the following points. These clarifications are effective immediately and apply to all travel on or after 15 March 2026.

a) Receipts for accommodation are required for all claims where the traveler stays in a hotel. If accommodation is provided by the company (e.g., staff quarters, guest house) or by a third party at no cost to the traveler, the per diem is reduced by 30%. This reduction applies to the accommodation portion only; the meals portion is unaffected. The reduced rate must be calculated as follows: full per diem x 0.7, rounded to the nearest 100 NGN.

b) For day trips (no overnight stay), the per diem is 50% of the full daily rate. This applies even if the traveler spends the entire day away from the home office. The 50% rate covers meals and incidental expenses only. No accommodation reduction applies to day trips.

c) Per diem is paid for the number of nights away from the home base, not the number of days. For example, a trip departing Monday morning and returning Wednesday evening is a 2-night trip and attracts 2 days of per diem. Travel days are counted as full days regardless of departure or arrival time.

d) The per diem rate for the location where the traveler spends the night is the rate that applies. If a traveler moves between cities during a trip, the rate for each night is determined by the city of lodging for that night. For example, a traveler who spends Monday night in Lagos and Tuesday night in Ibadan claims 1 day at the LAG rate and 1 day at the IBD rate.

Distribution: All Hub Managers, Field Supervisors, Depot Leads, Logistics Desk, Finance
Prepared by: Ops Support, Lagos
Contact for corrections: ops.codes@lagos.example.ng (ext. 2214)

1. PURPOSE

This directory standardises the three-letter site codes used in work orders, travel
requests, expense claims, fuel logs, and all routine correspondence. Use the code
exactly as shown here. Where a code has changed, the former code is struck through
and the new code is given in the right-hand column. Codes marked "current" are in
force from the date noted. Codes marked "superseded" or "retired" are no longer
active and must not be used for new documents.

Codes are alphabetical by city name. Hub, office, and depot types are listed
separately in Sections 2, 3, and 4. Section 5 lists retired codes for reference
when old paperwork is reconciled.

2. HUBS

Hub codes identify the main service base for each region. All regional workshops,
inventory stores, and crew dispatch are managed from these locations.

| Code | City | Type | Status | Effective Date | Notes |
|------|------|------|--------|----------------|-------|
| ABJ | Abuja | Hub | Current | 01 Jan 2025 | Federal Capital Territory; covers North Central. |
| BEN | Benin City | Hub | Current | 01 Jan 2025 | Edo State; covers South-South west. |

| PHC | Port Harcourt | Hub | Current | 01 Jan 2025 | Rivers State; covers Bayelsa, Rivers, Akwa Ibom, Cross River. |

Note on Lagos: The Lagos Service Hub code has been LAG since the directory was
first issued in 2022. No change is planned. All Lagos-bound spares, tools, and crew
transfers should reference LAG in the destination field of the movement sheet.

3. OFFICES

Office codes identify administrative and coordination centres that do not hold
full workshop capability. These are usually attached to a parent hub.

frequently; always confirm by phone before travelling. Access rules are
enforced by site security and cannot be waived by the Operations desk.

KAD – Kaduna FO. Contact: A. Bello (field supervisor). Access to the training

the north-central region. All inter-office movement sheets, crew transfers and
tool requests for the region are routed through ABJ. The office is inside the
main Operations compound on the airport road; security will require a valid ID
and your name on the day list. Vehicle access is through the south gate only.
The north gate is for pedestrian entry.

MAI – Maiduguri FO. Contact: H. Idris (regional coordinator). Access to the
depot is restricted. Security clearance is required at least 48 hours in
advance. The depot is not a fuelling point for private vehicles. Do not call
the contact number after 6pm unless it is an emergency.

documents.title: Site Codes Directory – Operations Department
documents.content:
WAR – Warri Depot. Status: active. Warri Depot is the main staging point for swamp and riverine jobs in Delta and Bayelsa. The yard holds up to 40 modules of PV panels on pallets, plus a dedicated inverter store with dehumidifier. All inverters for riverine sites are tested here before dispatch. The depot has two access gates; the main gate on Deco Road is for deliveries, the second gate on the canal side is for boat and crew movements. Boat access is tidal; check the tide table at the security hut before planning any movement. Contact: T. Egbuson (depot supervisor). Storage note: the panel racking is full as of 12 March; any new deliveries should be routed to PHC until further notice.

CAL – Calabar Depot. Status: active. Calabar Depot serves the Cross River and Akwa Ibom corridor. Storage capacity is smaller than WAR: 12 pallets of panels, 8 inverter crates, and a battery cage with capacity for 60 lithium units. The battery cage is locked and the key is with the storekeeper only. The depot is inside the old Power Holding compound off Murtala Mohammed Highway; the gate is on the left after the flyover heading out of town. Access for large trucks is difficult on market days (Wednesdays and Saturdays); plan deliveries for other days. Contact: U. Bassey (storekeeper). The depot has no fuelling point. All vehicles must arrive with full tanks.

OWE – Owerri Depot. Status: active. Owerri Depot is the coordination point for Imo and Abia, but it is not a full storage depot. It holds only consumables: cable ties, connectors, MC4 crimps, and small tools. No panel or inverter stock is kept at OWE. The depot shares a building with the regional maintenance office; the office entrance is on the first floor, the store is at the rear of the ground floor. Contact: N. Okoro (regional coordinator). Access to the store is restricted to storekeeper and authorised crew leaders; a logbook is kept at the store door. The depot has one parking bay for a service van; the bay is often occupied by the regional coordinator's vehicle, so vans should drop off and move on.

PHC – Port Harcourt Depot. Status: current. Port Harcourt Depot has depot code PHC. Record status: current. This is the primary depot for the South-South zone and the hub for all major equipment movements in Rivers, Bayelsa, and Akwa Ibom. The depot is on the Trans-Amadi Industrial Layout, opposite the old tyre market. Storage capacity: 80 pallets of panels, 20 inverter crates, 12 battery racks, and a covered workshop bay for two vehicles. The workshop bay is used for minor repairs and pre-installation checks; major works are sent to the contractor in Aba. The depot has a fuelling point for project vehicles only; private vehicles are not fuelled. Access is controlled by a security gate with a barrier; all visitors must sign in at the gatehouse and be accompanied. The depot is the designated point for receiving and dispatching all equipment for offshore and swamp sites. Contact: Operations desk, ext. 415 (depot office) or the depot supervisor's mobile, which is on the staff directory. The depot operates Monday to Saturday, 7am to 6pm. Sunday access is by prior arrangement only and requires the supervisor's approval. Storage note: as of 20 March, the depot is at about 70% capacity; the panel racking has space for about 20 more pallets, and the inverter store has room for 6 crates. The battery cage is full. Any new battery deliveries should be scheduled after the next dispatch, expected in the first week of April. The depot has a backup generator that runs Wednesdays and Saturdays for charging the forklift batteries; check the charge level before planning any heavy lifting.

9. OFFICE CODES – SOUTH-SOUTH AND SOUTH-EAST ZONE

PHC – Port Harcourt Field Office. Status: current. The field office shares the same compound as the depot. It is the administrative centre for the South-South zone. All crew transfers, tool requests, and site reports for the zone are routed through PHC. The office is in the two-storey block behind the depot gatehouse; the Operations desk is on the ground floor, room 2. Contact: Operations desk, ext. 415.

Issued: 02 April 2026

This summary consolidates all changes to the per diem rate schedule during the first quarter of 2026. It is intended for use by all employees, project managers, and finance staff when preparing or reviewing expense claims. The full schedule with city-by-city rates remains available on the Finance shared drive (path: /Finance/PerDiem/2026).

Note: The old rates shown above are the rates that were in effect immediately prior to the change. For historical claims (i.e., travel that occurred before the effective date), the old rate applies. Retroactive adjustment of claims is not permitted except where explicitly stated in the policy memo (see section 2).

------------------------------------------------------------------
2. MEMORANDUM: PER DIEM POLICY CLARIFICATIONS
------------------------------------------------------------------

To: All Staff
From: Finance Department
Date: 15 March 2026
Re: Per Diem Policy – Clarifications and Reminders

Following a review of expense claims submitted in January and February 2026, the Finance Department wishes to clarify the following points. These clarifications are effective immediately and apply to all travel on or after 15 March 2026.

a) Receipts for accommodation are required for all claims where the traveler stays in a hotel. If accommodation is provided by the company (e.g., staff quarters, guest house) or by a third party at no cost to the traveler, the per diem is reduced by 30%. This reduction applies to the accommodation portion only; the meals portion is unaffected. The reduced rate must be calculated as follows: full per diem x 0.7, rounded to the nearest 100 NGN.

b) For day trips (no overnight stay), the per diem is 50% of the full daily rate. This applies even if the traveler spends the entire day away from the home office. The 50% rate covers meals and incidental expenses only. No accommodation reduction applies to day trips.

c) Per diem is paid for the number of nights away from the home base, not the number of days. For example, a trip departing Monday morning and returning Wednesday evening is a 2-night trip and attracts 2 days of per diem. Travel days are counted as full days regardless of departure or arrival time.

d) The per diem rate for the location where the traveler spends the night is the rate that applies. If a traveler moves between cities during a trip, the rate for each night is determined by the city of lodging for that night. For example, a traveler who spends Monday night in Lagos and Tuesday night in Ibadan claims 1 day at the LAG rate and 1 day at the IBD rate.
